executive_summary: The Active Directory domain DOMAIN-1 exhibits a severely degraded security posture, holding a hygiene score of 1 out of 100, which indicates profound risk across multiple security domains. An intruder can leverage a combination of unpatched domain controller vulnerabilities (such as missing the noPac fix and weak Netlogon channels), insecure Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) templates permitting immediate privilege escalation, and exposed administrative rights including explicit DCSync permissions and writable SYSVOL objects. Furthermore, widespread operational negligence—such as weak or reused passwords, unrotated privileged credentials, and disabled SMB signing combined with unfiltered coercion interfaces—provides direct pathways to full domain compromise without requiring complex initial access. Immediate remediation must focus on patching critical domain controller vulnerabilities, revoking dangerous ACLs on the domain root, locking down AD CS certificate templates, and enforcing secure authentication protocols.

remediation_plan.title: Patch Domain Controllers and Enforce Secure Channels
remediation_plan.rationale: Addresses critical unpatched vulnerabilities on domain controllers and weak channel protections that allow trivial elevation of privilege and machine account impersonation.
remediation_plan.caveats: Test patches in a staging environment and ensure legacy clients support enforced LDAP signing and channel binding before deployment.

remediation_plan.title: Revoke Dangerous ACLs and DCSync Rights on Tier 0 Objects
remediation_plan.rationale: Removes unauthorized permissions granting non-Tier 0 principals the ability to perform DCSync, modify the domain root, or read sensitive attributes.
remediation_plan.caveats: Verify that removing permissions from the Exchange group or synchronization accounts does not disrupt core mail flow or directory synchronization functions.

remediation_plan.title: Secure AD CS Infrastructure and Disable Vulnerable Templates
remediation_plan.rationale: Hardens the Public Key Infrastructure by revoking overly permissive certificate templates, disabling unauthenticated web enrollment, and removing unauthorized CA management rights.
remediation_plan.caveats: Disabling web enrollment or modifying templates may impact applications relying on auto-enrollment; inventory template dependencies prior to removal.

remediation_plan.title: Clean Up SYSVOL, Group Policy Secrets, and Execution Paths
remediation_plan.rationale: Eliminates hardcoded credentials, group policy preferences passwords, and writable script paths that allow immediate code execution and privilege escalation.
remediation_plan.caveats: Review login scripts and GPO settings to ensure legitimate automated drive mappings or deployments are not broken by removing hardcoded credentials.

remediation_plan.title: Rotate Privileged Credentials and Enforce Strong Authentication
remediation_plan.rationale: Rotates stale krbtgt and privileged account passwords, fixes AS-REP roasting/Kerberoasting risks, and removes unauthorized shadow credentials.
remediation_plan.caveats: Rotating krbtgt requires two consecutive password changes to invalidate all existing Kerberos tickets gracefully.

quick_wins: Disable pre-authentication on accounts flagged for AS-REP roasting (USER-8, USER-19).
Disable the WebClient service on domain controllers to prevent WebDAV-based coercion.
Remove unauthorized permissions and excessive ACEs from the domain root and AdminSDHolder.
Enforce SMB signing and LDAP signing via Group Policy on all domain controllers.
Add critical administrative accounts and all Tier 0 members to the Protected Users group.

monitoring.guidance: Monitor for Directory Service Access events (4662) where the DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All extended right is invoked by non-standard accounts, and look for computer account modifications (4742) involving msDS-KeyCredentialLink changes.
Monitor AD CS Certificate Services audit events for certificate issuance requests (4887/4888) containing alternative subject names (SAN) requested by standard domain users.
Detect incoming NTLM authentications from domain controller computer accounts to other internal hosts or unexpected shares, indicating potential coercion and relay attacks.

attack_paths.title: AD CS ESC1 Certificate Enrollment
steps: TEMPLATE-1 -> Request certificate with arbitrary SAN
CA-1 -> Authenticate as Domain Admin via client auth certificate
attack_paths.narrative: Standard domain users can enroll in a misconfigured certificate template with enrollee-supplied subject settings and client authentication, allowing them to request a certificate for any administrative account and achieve full domain control.

attack_paths.title: DCSync via Explicit Rights
steps: NETBIOS-1\USER-31 -> Invoke DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All on domain head
attack_paths.narrative: A non-default user account holds explicit replication rights on the domain head, enabling the direct extraction of all domain credentials including krbtgt.

attack_paths.title: Shadow Credentials on Domain Controller
steps: DC-2$ -> Write key credential via msDS-KeyCredentialLink
Tier 0 (assumed) -> Authenticate as DC via Public Key Cryptography
attack_paths.narrative: An active key credential set on a domain controller object permits an intruder to authenticate as the DC and compromise the entire domain.

attack_paths.title: Kerberoasting Privileged Accounts
steps: USER-6 -> Request TGS for Kerberoastable SPN
Tier 0 (assumed) -> Log in as Domain Admin
attack_paths.narrative: Privileged accounts with registered Service Principal Names and weak or old passwords can be targeted for offline ticket cracking to recover administrative credentials.

attack_paths.title: Writable SYSVOL Group Policy Preferences
attack_paths.narrative: Writable SYSVOL or embedded Group Policy Preferences passwords allow attackers to extract plaintext credentials or inject malicious scripts executed by domain controllers.

attack_paths.title: Coercion and NTLM Relay
steps: DCHOST-2 -> Coerce authentication via open RPC / WebClient interfaces
LDAP / AD CS -> Relay NTLM to unencrypted endpoints
Tier 0 (assumed) -> Issue administrative certificate or object modification
attack_paths.narrative: Open coercion interfaces on domain controllers combined with unencrypted LDAP and vulnerable AD CS web enrollment allow NTLM relay attacks resulting in domain compromise.

remediation_scripts.caveats: Test thoroughly; disabling anonymous authentication on web enrollment may require adjusting client authentication methods.
Ensure no business-critical applications on the domain controllers rely on WebDAV functionality.

triage.rationale: Provide immediate, unauthenticated paths to forge administrative certificates and achieve domain control.
Grant explicit replication and modification rights over Tier 0 objects, enabling instant credential harvesting.
Critical remote code execution and elevation flaws on domain controllers that bypass standard authentication controls.
Active persistence mechanisms and delegation misconfigurations directly targeting domain controllers.
Exposes cleartext administrative credentials and allows arbitrary file modification within SYSVOL.

known_exploitation.public: Widely reported in ransomware intrusions by multiple threat actor groups to escalate from standard user to Domain Admin.
known_exploitation.relevance: DCHOST-2 lacks the security update and machine account quotas permit rapid computer object manipulation.

known_exploitation.vector: AD CS ESC1 and ESC8 NTLM Relay
known_exploitation.public: Extensively documented vector in enterprise compromises and ransomware campaigns leading to immediate domain dominance.
known_exploitation.relevance: TEMPLATE-1 allows enrollee-supplied subjects for low-privileged users, and CA-1 runs vulnerable web enrollment.

known_exploitation.public: Frequently utilized in initial access and internal lateral movement to reset domain controller machine passwords to empty strings.
known_exploitation.relevance: Domain Controllers have weakened secure channel enforcement.

known_exploitation.public: A staple of internal penetration testing and automated post-exploitation tooling for harvesting credentials from SYSVOL.
known_exploitation.relevance: GPO contains cpassword artifacts within PATH-1.

compromise_assessment.summary: The environment contains multiple independent, reliable escalation chains allowing any standard domain user to achieve full domain control without requiring prior administrative privileges.

chains.title: AD CS ESC1 Certificate Escalation

break_point.why: Revoke enrollment permissions for low-privileged users and disable enrollee-supplied subject names.

chains.narrative: A low-privileged domain user requests a certificate via TEMPLATE-1 specifying a Domain Admin principal in the SAN, authenticates to the domain controllers, and achieves instant domain compromise.

chains.title: Explicit DCSync Rights Escalation

break_point.why: Remove DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All extended right from unauthorized principals.

chains.narrative: Compromise of USER-31 grants direct DCSync capabilities to harvest all domain password hashes and take over the domain.

chains.title: noPac Vulnerability Exploitation

break_point.why: Apply the official security updates for CVE-2021-42278 and CVE-2021-42287 on DCHOST-2.

chains.narrative: Utilizing the machine account quota, an attacker creates a computer object, renames it to impersonate a domain controller, and exploits unpatched validation logic to acquire administrative tickets.

chains.title: SYSVOL GPP Credential Harvesting

break_point.why: Remove GPO files containing cpassword entries from SYSVOL.

chains.narrative: Any domain user reading SYSVOL can decrypt stored Group Policy Preferences passwords and use them to authenticate as an administrator.

rejected_chains.title: Unauthenticated Domain Takeover via Anonymous LDAP
rejected_chains.reason: While anonymous LDAP search is enabled, anonymous users cannot directly modify domain objects or read sensitive credentials without additional privilege links.

rejected_chains.title: Exchange PrivExchange Relay to Domain Controller
rejected_chains.reason: Relies on an Exchange server presence and specific active service configurations that are not fully validated as reachable targets in this topology snapshot.

verify_next.question: Are all domain controllers actively patched against CVE-2021-42278 and CVE-2021-42287?
Can standard users successfully query and enroll in certificate template TEMPLATE-1?
Is SMB signing enforced on workstation and server network adapters across the domain?
Are the accounts flagged with pre-authentication disabled actively monitored or utilized by legacy applications?
